question.problem: Let $f(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y.$ Given that $C$ is the path along the curve $y=2x$ for  $x\in [0,\pi ],$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a piecewise-smooth curve given by the vector function $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b].$ Let $f$ be a differentiable function of two or three variables such that $∇f$ is continuous on $C.$ The fundamental theorem for line integrals states that 

$$
{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r=f(r(b))-f(r(a)).
$$

We start by parametrizing the curve $C.$ A suitable parametrization is

$$
r(t)=⟨t,2t⟩,\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$

Then, the position vectors of the endpoints of the curve are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨0,0⟩ \\ r(\pi ) & =⟨\pi ,2\pi ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the endpoints of the path defined by $C$ are $(0,0)$ and $(\pi ,2\pi ).$

Applying the fundamental theorem for line integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r & =f(r(\pi ))-f(r(0)) \\  & =f(\pi ,2\pi )-f(0,0) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi )-(\operatorname{sin}⁡0+\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =(0+1)-(0+1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
